Name: Restart-WinProcess.ps1
Description: Stops a named process. If the -Start switch is supplied the process is also restarted after stopping. Process name must be provided as an input.
Impact Notes: Stopping the wrong process can crash applications with unsaved data or destabilise the user session. No validation or safelist is applied before stopping.
Additional Notes: Consider adding a safelist of processes that should never be stopped

Name: Restart-WinService.ps1
Description: Stops and restarts a named Windows service. Service name must be provided as an input.
Impact Notes: Service restart may briefly interrupt functionality provided by that service.

Name: Restart-WindowsUpdateServices.ps1
Description: Stops and restarts Windows Update and related services (wuauserv / BITS / cryptsvc / msiserver) to resolve stalled or broken update states. Supports a -ForceRestart switch.
Impact Notes: Services are temporarily unavailable during restart. No user-visible interruption unless an update was actively installing.

Name: Enable-HardwareAcceleratedGPUScheduling.ps1
Description: Enables Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS) via the registry. Reduces CPU overhead for GPU-heavy workloads. Requires Windows 10 2004+ and a WDDM 2.7+ GPU driver. A reboot is required for the change to take effect.
Impact Notes: Requires a reboot. May cause display instability on devices with drivers that do not fully support WDDM 2.7+.

Name: Disable-NonEssentialStartupApps.ps1
Description: Removes non-essential applications from the Windows startup sequence via Run registry keys and StartupApproved keys.
Impact Notes: User startup apps are disabled without notification. Users may be surprised that apps they configured no longer auto-launch at logon.
Additional Notes: Define which apps are considered non-essential before deploying at scale

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateAudioBluetooth.ps1
Description: Runs sequenced audio and Bluetooth health checks and automatically remediates failures: restarts audio services (AudioSrv / AudioEndpointBuilder), refreshes errored PnP audio devices, corrects microphone access policy, and ensures the Bluetooth service is running.
Impact Notes: Audio service restarts cause a ~1-2 second interruption. Volume mute-state correction sends a keyboard keystroke. No dialogs or user prompts.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateDriverIssues.ps1
Description: Runs sequenced driver health checks across audio / Bluetooth / network adapter classes. Remediates via an escalating action chain controlled by -AllowedActions (Scan / Restart / Rollback / Reinstall / Uninstall) and scoped by -DriverFilter regex. Default actions are Scan + Restart + Rollback.
Impact Notes: Destructive actions (Reinstall / Uninstall) permanently remove devices from the PnP tree with no undo. A misconfigured -DriverFilter can remove network adapters leaving the device unreachable via MDM.
Additional Notes: Use default actions only unless a specific issue requires escalation. Test -DriverFilter patterns in a lab first. Never deploy Reinstall/Uninstall to NICs at scale.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateNetworkStack.ps1
Description: Automated network stack diagnostic and remediation. Checks and remediates network adapter state, TCP/IP stack health, DNS client service, and basic connectivity.
Impact Notes: Network stack reset operations briefly disrupt all network connectivity. DNS flush and adapter restart cause a short gap in network availability.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediatePrinter.ps1
Description: Runs sequenced printer health checks (Print Spooler service / installed printers / offline state / default printer / queue health / driver status) and automatically remediates failures where possible.
Impact Notes: Print Spooler service restart cancels in-flight print jobs. Users must resubmit queued jobs after the remediation.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateFSLogixExclusions.ps1
Description: Applies Microsoft's documented Windows Defender exclusions for FSLogix profile containers (frxccd / frxccds / frxsvc processes, Cache and Proxy paths, temp and profile-share VHD/VHDX paths, VHD and VHDX extensions). VHD locations are read from FSLogix's own VHDLocations configuration rather than hard-coded. Addresses slow FSLogix attach at logon caused by real-time AV scanning of open container handles.
Impact Notes: Only adds antivirus exclusions; removes nothing and touches no user data. Exits without changes when FSLogix is not installed or when Defender cmdlets are unavailable.
Additional Notes: Defender only. Third-party AV needs the same exclusions set through its own console or policy. Supports WhatIf via the WhatIf environment variable. Results written to HKLM:\Software\AirWatch\Extensions\FSLogix\Remediation.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateProfileBloat.ps1
Description: Trims the per-user cache data that inflates user profile load time at logon (user temp files, Chrome/Edge/Firefox caches, Teams cache, Explorer thumbnail and icon caches, crash dumps and error reports, RDP and shader caches, Recent items and jump lists). Also reports, without remediating, oversized roaming AppData and oversized NTUSER.DAT/UsrClass.dat hives.
Impact Notes: Deletes only regenerable caches older than a configurable age, so applications rebuild them on next use. Never touches Documents, Desktop, Downloads, bookmarks, browser history, saved credentials, Outlook data files, or signatures. Files locked by a live session are skipped rather than forced. Clearing Recent items and jump lists is user-visible.
Additional Notes: Parameters MinFileAgeDays (7), MinSizeThresholdMB (50), RoamingWarnMB (500) and HiveWarnMB (100) default from same-named environment variables; explicit parameters win. Supports WhatIf via the WhatIf environment variable, which is the recommended first run. Complements DiskCleanup\Start-UserProfileCleanup.ps1 (deletes whole inactive profiles) rather than duplicating it. Results written to HKLM:\Software\AirWatch\Extensions\ProfileBloat\Remediation.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateLogonTaskContention.ps1
Description: Staggers third-party scheduled tasks that trigger At Log On (adds/raises each qualifying trigger's Delay) so they stop competing with the shell, Group Policy, and profile load for CPU and disk during logon. Also reports, without remediating, when the total count of logon-triggered tasks exceeds a warn threshold.
Impact Notes: Only adds or increases a trigger's Delay; never disables, deletes, or changes what a task does. Only touches tasks outside the built-in \Microsoft\ Task Scheduler namespace -- OS-owned tasks are never modified. Delaying a task changes when it runs, which could matter for a task with a genuine time-sensitivity the script cannot know about.
Additional Notes: Parameters MinDelaySeconds (60), StaggerSeconds (30) and TaskVolumeWarnCount (8) default from same-named environment variables; explicit parameters win. Supports WhatIf via the WhatIf environment variable, which is the recommended first run. Pairs with the LogonTaskCount/LogonTaskTotalDurationSec fields from Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 (GenericTroubleshooting/WindowsStartup), though this script is self-contained and does not require it to have run first. Results written to HKLM:\Software\AirWatch\Extensions\LogonTaskContention\Remediation.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateAppXBloat.ps1
Description: Deprovisions non-essential inbox AppX packages (Xbox companion apps, Solitaire, Weather, News, People, Mixed Reality Portal, Messaging, Skype, Feedback Hub, 3D tools, Maps, Wallet, Family Safety, Clipchamp) via a curated deny list, reducing AppReadiness registration load at logon. Optionally also removes matching packages already installed for existing users.
Impact Notes: A hard-coded safelist (Calculator, Camera, Notepad, Paint, Snip & Sketch, Store, Photos, Terminal, To Do, Widgets host, Defender UI, shell/framework components) cannot be overridden by DenyListExtra, so core apps are never removed. Deprovisioning (default behavior) only affects new user profiles created afterward -- no visible impact to existing users. Enabling RemoveForExistingUsers additionally removes matching Start Menu tiles from already-installed profiles.
Additional Notes: Parameters DenyListExtra (comma-separated wildcard patterns) and RemoveForExistingUsers (default false) default from same-named environment variables; explicit parameters win. Supports WhatIf via the WhatIf environment variable, which is the recommended first run. Complements UnmanagedAppReport\Get-StartupApps.ps1 (Run-key/Startup-folder apps only, not AppX) rather than duplicating it. Results written to HKLM:\Software\AirWatch\Extensions\AppXBloat\Remediation.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateWindowsUpdates.ps1
Description: Runs sequenced Windows Update health checks (WU / BITS / Cryptographic services / DataStore / pending reboot / policy). Automatically remediates service failures and optionally clears a corrupt DataStore.
Impact Notes: Services are briefly stopped and restarted. DataStore reset clears update history. Pending reboot is flagged but never forced.

Name: Invoke-SimpleReboot.ps1
Description: Displays a configurable countdown notification to the logged-on user then forces a reboot via shutdown.exe. Default countdown is 5 minutes.
Impact Notes: Forces a reboot after countdown. Unsaved work will be lost if the user does not act on the notification.

Name: Invoke_RebootWithUserDefer_1.2.0.7.ps1
Description: Advanced reboot orchestrator that notifies the user on a configurable schedule and forces a reboot after a maximum deferral window expires. Configurable countdown duration, notification interval, and maximum deferral hours.
Impact Notes: Reboot is ultimately forced after the max deferral window. Unsaved work will be lost if the user ignores all notifications.

Name: SmartReboot.ps1
Description: Detection component for the SmartReboot workflow. Checks the AirWatch SmartReboot registry key to determine if a pending install has completed. Returns exit 1641 (install pending) or 0 (complete).
Impact Notes: Detection only - does not initiate a reboot itself.
Additional Notes: Used as a detection script in WS1 to gate reboot-required logic

Name: Get-UserProfileSize.ps1
Description: Reports the size of all user profiles on the device. Useful for identifying disk space consumed by inactive or oversized profiles before running cleanup scripts.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.

Name: Start-ClearRecycleBin.ps1
Description: Empties the Recycle Bin for all user profiles on the device silently.
Impact Notes: Permanently deletes Recycle Bin contents. Users cannot recover deleted files after this runs.

Name: Start-DiskCleanup.ps1
Description: Automates Windows Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr.exe) targeting system-level categories: previous Windows installations, update artifacts, error dumps, and upgrade logs. Reports GB reclaimed on completion.
Impact Notes: Deletes system cleanup categories which cannot be recovered. Previous Windows installation data is permanently removed.

Name: Start-UserProfileCleanup.ps1
Description: Removes inactive user profiles from the device based on configurable inactivity period (days) and size threshold (MB). Skips the configured enrollment user account.
Impact Notes: Deletes user profiles - all local data in those profiles is permanently lost. Misconfiguring the enrollment user exclusion can result in unintended profile deletion.
Additional Notes: Requires admin to configure ENROLLMENTUSER, DAYS_INACTIVE, and SIZE_THRESHOLD_MB before deploying

Name: Get-StartupApps.ps1
Description: Enumerates all startup entries for the currently logged-on user from 64-bit and 32-bit Run registry keys, startup folders, and Task Scheduler logon-trigger tasks. Reports name, enabled/disabled state, command, source, and user.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Runs as SYSTEM using SID-based registry access to target the logged-on user hive

Name: DEX_Invoke-SignoffWindows.ps1
Description: Signs off user sessions on a managed Windows device. Defaults to all sessions; use -CurrentUser switch to target only the active console session.
Impact Notes: Signs off user sessions - all unsaved work is lost. Ensure user notification is in place before deploying.

Name: DEX_LockDevice-BitlockEncryptionActivated.ps1
Description: Disables BitLocker protectors on C: then immediately initiates a hard shutdown. Intended for device decommission or emergency scenarios where encryption must be suspended before power-off.
Impact Notes: Forces an immediate shutdown - all unsaved work is lost. BitLocker protectors are disabled meaning the drive can be read without a recovery key until protectors are re-enabled.
Additional Notes: Use only for device decommission or specific security scenarios. Understand BitLocker implications before deploying.

Name: DEX_Start-LockDeviceSoft.ps1
Description: Soft-locks the active console session using tsdiscon.exe. Disconnects and locks the screen without signing the user out - all running processes and unsaved work are preserved.
Impact Notes: Screen is locked and session disconnected. User processes continue running in the background. No data loss.

Name: sensor-getservice.ps1
Description: Returns a JSON-compressed list of all currently running Windows services. Lightweight DEX sensor for service inventory and health monitoring.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.

Name: Invoke-DefenderServiceRemediation.ps1
Description: Ensures core Microsoft Defender services (MDCoreSvc / WinDefend / WdNisSvc / mpssvc) are set to Automatic startup and running. Re-enables Real-Time Protection if it has been disabled.
Impact Notes: Service restarts may cause a brief gap in protection. Real-Time Protection toggling is instantaneous with no user-visible effect.

Name: Invoke-DefenderPauseScan.ps1
Description: Locates the highest available version of MpCmdRun.exe from the Defender platform directory and issues a scan cancel command. Safe to run when no scan is active.
Impact Notes: Cancels an active scan - scan progress is lost and must be re-triggered separately.

Name: Invoke-DefenderDynamicPerformance.ps1
Description: Calculates a hardware performance score from BIOS generation date, CPU core count, and system disk type (HDD/SSD/NVMe). Maps the score to a Defender CPU profile (VeryLow/Low/Medium/High) and applies matching ScanAvgCPULoadFactor and EnableLowCpuPriority settings via Set-MpPreference.
Impact Notes: Modifies Defender scan CPU thresholds only. No user-visible interruption.
Additional Notes: Useful for dynamically tuning Defender without assigning multiple MDM profiles per hardware tier

Name: Invoke-DefenderEnableCloudBlock_BAFS.ps1
Description: Enables Defender cloud protection settings: CloudBlockLevel (High/1), MAPSReporting (Advanced), and SubmitSamplesConsent (1 = send safe samples). All changes are idempotent and only applied if not already at the target value.
Impact Notes: No user-visible interruption. Increases cloud telemetry sent to Microsoft. Confirm SubmitSamplesConsent is appropriate for your data classification requirements.
Additional Notes: Confirm SubmitSamplesConsent is acceptable in regulated/restricted environments before deploying

Name: Invoke-DefenderUpdateSignatures.ps1
Description: Checks whether Defender virus definitions are out of date. If so triggers Update-MpSignature as a background job so the script exits within MDM timeout windows.
Impact Notes: Background signature update consumes network bandwidth. No user-visible interruption during script execution.

Name: Start-DefenderThreatReport_1.4.8.4.ps1
Description: Queries active Defender threats and maps detected threat names to the Windows Uninstall registry for reporting in Workspace ONE Intelligence. Threat records are persisted for a configurable number of hours.
Impact Notes: Registry write only - no remediation actions taken. Threat data written to the Uninstall key may appear as installed apps in some reporting views.
Additional Notes: Designed to run on a recurring trigger (every 4 hours) for near-real-time threat visibility in Intelligence

Name: defender_cloudblock_bafs.ps1
Description: Detection sensor: reports the current Defender Block-at-First-Sight (BAFS) and cloud protection state (CloudBlockLevel / MAPSReporting / SubmitSamplesConsent).
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.

Name: defender_computerstate_summary.ps1
Description: Detection sensor: reports a summary of Microsoft Defender computer protection state including RTP status, signature age, scan status, and service health.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.

Name: defender_licensestatus.ps1
Description: Detection sensor: reports Microsoft Defender for Endpoint license and onboarding state via the OnboardingState registry key.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.

Name: defender_signatureoutofdate.ps1
Description: Detection sensor: reports whether Microsoft Defender virus definition signatures are out of date via Get-MpComputerStatus.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.

Name: Invoke-CrowdStrikeServiceRemediation.ps1
Description: Ensures CrowdStrike Falcon services are running and set to Automatic startup. Note: Falcon is tamper-protected and cloud-managed - service remediation may be blocked by design. Confirm with your security team before deploying.
Impact Notes: CrowdStrike service restart may cause a brief gap in endpoint protection. Falcon tamper protection may actively block service state changes.
Additional Notes: Verify with security team that service remediation is permitted in your Falcon policy before deploying

Name: Invoke-TrellixCPUPriority.ps1
Description: Sets Trellix (formerly McAfee) endpoint security processes to BelowNormal CPU priority to reduce performance impact during active scans. Priority change is in-process only and does not persist across service restarts.
Impact Notes: CPU priority change is transparent to the user. No service interruption.
Additional Notes: Lab-tested only - validate in production before broad deployment

Name: Invoke-TrellixLocalUpdate.ps1
Description: Forces a local content update for Trellix Endpoint Security (amcfg.exe /update) then triggers a policy refresh via CmdAgent.exe. Supports both McAfee and Trellix installation paths.
Impact Notes: Update and policy refresh run in the background. No user-visible interruption.
Additional Notes: Lab-tested only - validate in production before broad deployment

Name: Invoke-TrellixRefreshPolicies.ps1
Description: Forces a policy refresh for Trellix (formerly McAfee) Endpoint Security via CmdAgent.exe steps: collect/send properties, send events, and check for new policies.
Impact Notes: Policy refresh runs in the background. No user-visible interruption.
Additional Notes: Lab-tested only - validate in production before broad deployment

Name: Invoke-TrendMicroServiceRemediation.ps1
Description: Ensures Trend Micro Apex One / OfficeScan services (ntrtscan / tmlisten / ofcservice / TmCCSF / TmWSCSvc / TmPfw) are running and set to Automatic startup.
Impact Notes: Trend Micro service restart may cause a brief gap in endpoint protection.
Additional Notes: Lab-tested only - validate in production before broad deployment

Name: performance_bitlockerstatus.ps1
Description: Detection sensor: reports the BitLocker protection status and encryption state of the C: drive.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.

Name: performance_defender_scanorupdateactive.ps1
Description: Detection sensor: reports whether a Microsoft Defender scan or signature update is currently active. Useful for correlating Defender activity with high-CPU events in DEX.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.

Name: performance_windowsupdate_status.ps1
Description: Detection sensor: reports the current Windows Update activity status (Idle / Downloading / Installing / etc.).
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.

Name: performance_internetspeedtest.ps1
Description: One-time/run-once sensor: measures live download and upload throughput (Mbps) against Cloudflare's public speed-test endpoints, self-deadlined per phase, and reports both as a compact JSON string.
Impact Notes: Read-only - generates transient network traffic (~a few MB up/down) for the duration of the test only. MUST be deployed as a one-time/run-once sensor, never a recurring schedule.
Additional Notes: Run-once sensor delivery required (see GENERAL-SCRIPTS-SENSORS_RUNBOOK.md \u00a710, One-Time / Run-Once Sensors)

Name: Measure-GPLoadTime.ps1
Description: Records Group Policy Client Side Extension (CSE) load times for the logged-on user to the registry. Mines the Microsoft-Windows-GroupPolicy event log for the most recent GP cycle and captures total duration and top 5 slowest CSEs.
Impact Notes: Read and registry write only. No user-visible interruption. Designed to run at logon via a SYSTEM scheduled task.

Name: Measure-GPLoadTimeEx.ps1
Description: Extended version of Measure-GPLoadTime with additional metric collection and GPO correlation detail.
Impact Notes: Read and registry write only. No user-visible interruption.

Name: Measure-LogonDuration.ps1
Description: Records logon duration phases (total, Group Policy, GP scripts, folder redirection, profile load, FSLogix attach, ActiveSetup, AppX, printer mapping, logon tasks) for the logged-on user to the registry by mining event logs. DeployMode (RunNow / DeployScheduledTask / ConfigureLogging) and ConfigureLoggingFirst are parameters that default from matching environment variables, so UEM can configure via script variables while a caller can still override with explicit parameters.
Impact Notes: Read and registry write only. Optional event log enablement (PrintService/Operational, TaskScheduler/Operational) is a config toggle, not a device-facing change. No user-visible interruption.
Additional Notes: See Measure-LogonDuration-UEM-Deployment.md for full UEM console setup. Printer/task phases report LogDisabled until ConfigureLogging step is run.

Name: Measure-LogonDurationEx.ps1
Description: Extended version of Measure-LogonDuration with additional logon phase coverage and metric detail.
Impact Notes: Read and registry write only. No user-visible interruption.

Name: logon_username.ps1
Description: Reports the DOMAIN\User whose logon the cached timings belong to. Empty string when the collector has not run.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_time.ps1
Description: Reports the local time the session logon began (EID 4624 / TerminalServices EID 21) as the start point for total logon duration. Date Time type; no value emitted when unavailable -- there is no safe sentinel date.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_shell_ready_time.ps1
Description: Reports the local time the user's shell became ready (Winlogon EID 7001) -- the end point for total logon duration. Date Time type; no value emitted when unavailable.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_total_duration_ms.ps1
Description: Reports total logon duration in milliseconds, from session logon to shell ready. Integer sensor; UEM has no decimal type, so ms preserves sub-second resolution that whole-second rounding would erase.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_gp_start_time.ps1
Description: Reports the local time Group Policy user processing began (GP EID 4001). Date Time type; no value emitted when unavailable.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_gp_duration_ms.ps1
Description: Reports total Group Policy user processing time in milliseconds (GP EID 4001 -> 8001), usually the largest contributor to a slow domain-joined logon.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_gp_scripts_duration_ms.ps1
Description: Reports time spent running Group Policy logon scripts in milliseconds (GP EID 4018 -> 5018, ScriptType=1), isolated from total GP time.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_folder_redirect_duration_ms.ps1
Description: Reports Folder Redirection processing time in milliseconds (EID 501 -> 502) across all redirected folders. Sensitive to file server latency.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_profile_load_duration_ms.ps1
Description: Reports user profile load time in milliseconds (User Profile Service EID 1 -> 2). Pair with Get-UserProfileSize.ps1 to distinguish a big profile from a slow storage path.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_fslogix_attach_duration_ms.ps1
Description: Reports FSLogix profile container attach time in milliseconds. Returns -2 (not applicable) on any device without FSLogix installed, which is expected on a physical fleet.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_activesetup_duration_ms.ps1
Description: Reports ActiveSetup duration in milliseconds (Shell-Core EID 62170 -> 62171). Typically near zero except on first logon after an application deployment.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_appx_load_duration_ms.ps1
Description: Reports AppX / UWP package staging time in milliseconds at logon (AppReadiness EID 209). Notable on Windows 11 images carrying a large inbox app set.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 to have run at least once.

Name: logon_printers_mapped_count.ps1
Description: Reports the number of network printer connections established at logon (PrintService EID 300). -3 (log disabled) is the expected first result -- PrintService/Operational is off by default.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires PrintService/Operational log enabled -- run Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 with DeployMode ConfigureLogging.

Name: logon_printer_mapping_duration_ms.ps1
Description: Reports time spent mapping network printers at logon in milliseconds (PrintService EID 300 -> 306). -3 (log disabled) is the expected first result.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires PrintService/Operational log enabled -- run Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 with DeployMode ConfigureLogging.

Name: logon_task_count.ps1
Description: Reports the number of scheduled tasks that started within five minutes of logon (EID 100). A high count is directly actionable -- these tasks can be rescheduled away from the logon window.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires TaskScheduler/Operational log enabled -- run Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 with DeployMode ConfigureLogging.

Name: logon_task_total_duration_ms.ps1
Description: Reports the span in milliseconds from the first scheduled task start to the last completion within five minutes of logon (EID 100 -> 102) -- contention with the user's first actions, not a logon phase.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled. Requires TaskScheduler/Operational log enabled -- run Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 with DeployMode ConfigureLogging.

Name: logon_data_collected_at.ps1
Description: Reports the local time the collector last wrote its results -- the freshness check for every other logon duration sensor. Date Time type; no value emitted when the collector has never run.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Alert on staleness here before trusting any other sensor in this group.

Name: logon_duration_summary.ps1
Description: Returns every logon phase timing as a single compressed JSON object (String sensor). Use instead of the 17 individual sensors when consuming downstream; use the individual sensors when charting or thresholding directly.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Returns {"CollectorPresent":false} when Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 has never run. UEM cannot threshold on values inside a JSON string.

Name: Restart-WinProcessGraceful.ps1
Description: Gracefully closes (and optionally restarts) a Windows process matched by FileDescription, protecting unsaved user work. A thin launcher returns to Hub in ~1-2 s and self-extracts a detached watchdog owned by Task Scheduler; the watchdog runs in the logged-on user session (required -- as SYSTEM in session 0 MainWindowHandle is always zero, so responsiveness cannot be measured and a restart would launch invisibly). Sends CloseMainWindow/WM_CLOSE, or taskkill without /F for windowless processes, then polls each target once per second. Outcomes: ClosedGracefully, ForceKilled, UserActionRequired, UnsavedWorkSuspected, Error.
Impact Notes: Graceful termination gives the process a chance to save state, but if escalation reaches force-kill, unsaved work may be lost. In SYSTEM context, cross-session WM_CLOSE is blocked by UIPI; taskkill is the effective graceful path.
Additional Notes: A RESPONDING process is never force-killed: still open at the deadline means the app is showing a save prompt, so it is left running, reported UserActionRequired, and re-attempted up to UserActionRetryCount times (default 1) with UserActionRetryDelaySec between attempts (default 300 s, polled every 5 s so a user who closes the app during the wait is never re-signalled). Force-kill is reserved for a process confirmed hung -- UnresponsiveSampleCount consecutive non-responding checks, streak reset on recovery, so a slow save is not misread as a hang. With no user logged on the watchdog falls back to SYSTEM and NEVER force-kills, since unmeasurable must not mean hung. Optional SkipIfUnsavedWork leaves a process whose window title carries a modified-document marker entirely untouched (UnsavedWorkSuspected); the hint is recorded either way but is a hint, never proof, and can only make the script more cautious. Office ~$ owner files deliberately not probed -- they mean a document is open, not dirty. Exit code reflects DISPATCH, not the close outcome; read state\result.json or the companion sensor. Requires an AV/EDR exclusion on C:\ProgramData\AirWatch\Extensions\ProcessGraceful. Architecture and rationale in ProcessManagement\README.md.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateAllDriverIssues.ps1
Description: Full-sweep variant of Invoke-AutoRemediateDriverIssues that scans all defined PnP device classes (audio, Bluetooth, network, display, input, storage) for driver error codes and applies an escalating remediation sequence controlled by -AllowedActions. Device class coverage is table-driven -- no code changes required to add or remove classes.
Impact Notes: Destructive actions (Reinstall / Uninstall) permanently remove devices from the PnP tree with no undo. Covers all device classes -- wider blast radius than the targeted variant. Never deploy Reinstall/Uninstall to NICs at scale.
Additional Notes: Use default actions only (Scan + Restart + Rollback) unless a specific issue requires escalation. Test -DriverFilter patterns in a lab first.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateWiFiSignalIssues.ps1
Description: Runs sequenced Wi-Fi health checks (adapter detection / signal strength / driver age / NIC power management / adapter power saving mode / power plan wireless settings / USB selective suspend) and automatically remediates failures. Bounces the adapter if signal is below the warning threshold. Corrects power management settings that throttle wireless performance.
Impact Notes: Adapter bounce (disable/enable) causes a 10-30 second Wi-Fi reconnection interruption. Power plan and adapter power management changes persist after the script runs. Driver age check is informational only.
Additional Notes: Deploy AdapterName via env var to target a specific NIC; defaults to auto-detect on 802.11 media type.

Name: Invoke-DriverUpdates.ps1
Description: Queries Windows Update for available driver updates, optionally filtered by title regex, and in Install mode downloads and installs up to a configurable cap. Detect mode exits 1 (non-compliant) if updates are found. Reports reboot requirement via exit code 3010 without forcing a reboot. High-risk driver classes (audio / GPU / USB / chipset / storage) always set the reboot flag.
Impact Notes: Driver installation may cause brief device interruption per driver class. The script never initiates a reboot; a separate reboot workflow must handle exit code 3010.
Additional Notes: Deploy in Detect mode first to inventory pending updates before switching to Install mode at scale.

Name: Invoke-RemediateMemoryCompression.ps1
Description: Detects and remediates disabled Windows Memory Compression via the MMAgent. If compression is disabled, enables it with Enable-MMAgent -MemoryCompression. No reboot required. Writes scan result to the HKLM DEXRecords registry key for DEX reporting.
Impact Notes: No user-visible interruption. MMAgent change takes effect without a reboot.

Name: Invoke-RemediatePageFile.ps1
Description: Detects whether the Windows page file is manually configured (fixed size) and whether usage exceeds the configurable threshold. If the page file is not system-managed and is at the failure threshold, resets it to system-managed via CIM. High usage on a system-managed page file is reported but not changed. Writes scan result to the HKLM DEXRecords registry key.
Impact Notes: Page file configuration change requires a reboot to take full effect. System-managed page file with high usage is informational only -- a signal to review physical RAM.

Name: Invoke-RemediateSysMain.ps1
Description: Detects and remediates a stopped or disabled SysMain (Superfetch) service. Sets the startup type to Automatic and starts the service if it is not running. Writes scan result to the HKLM DEXRecords registry key for DEX reporting.
Impact Notes: No user-visible interruption. On SSD-only devices where SysMain is intentionally disabled, apply device targeting before deploying.
Additional Notes: Verify SysMain is not intentionally disabled by policy before deploying at scale.

Name: Start-DefenderFullScan.ps1
Description: Triggers a Microsoft Defender full scan via the MpCmdRun.exe platform binary with a configurable maximum scan duration. Uses a randomised run event ID for scan tracking. Does not wait for scan completion -- exits after initiating the scan.
Impact Notes: Initiates a full Defender scan which consumes CPU and disk I/O for the scan duration. No remediation actions taken.
Additional Notes: Filename contains a typo ('Scane') retained for compatibility.

Name: startup_app_list.ps1
Description: Reports installed applications from the Windows Uninstall registry alongside startup entries for the logged-on user. Combines HKLM Uninstall data with user-context startup keys to produce a unified app and startup inventory for DEX unmanaged application reporting.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Runs as SYSTEM using SID-based registry access to target the logged-on user hive.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateOutlook.ps1
Description: Runs sequenced Outlook-specific health checks and remediates where possible. Covers third-party add-in conflict detection (LoadBehavior), OST cache size threshold, Exchange sync backlog (event log), C2R update health, and Outlook profile integrity. Process health, network, disk, and Windows Update steps are intentionally excluded -- handled by generic scripts.
Impact Notes: OST rename (gated by $AllowDestructiveActions) forces a full mailbox resync which may consume significant bandwidth. Add-in disable (gated) removes Outlook integration for that add-in until re-enabled by IT.
Additional Notes: Set $AllowDestructiveActions=$true via env var to enable OST rename and add-in disable. Default is safe/read-mostly.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateTeams.ps1
Description: Runs sequenced Teams-specific health checks supporting both Classic Teams (Electron/Update.exe) and New Teams (MSTeams AppX) -- detects which variant is installed and runs applicable checks. Covers cache bloat, sign-in/auth token cache, stuck updater process, update log health, notification settings, and New Teams AppX package registration health.
Impact Notes: Auth token cache clear (gated by $AllowDestructiveActions) forces Teams re-login on next launch. New Teams AppX re-registration (gated) resets local Teams state. General cache clear runs automatically when Teams is not running.
Additional Notes: Reports TeamsVariant (Classic / New / both) to the DEXRecords registry key for inventory visibility.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateChrome.ps1
Description: Runs sequenced Chrome-specific health checks. Automatically clears Cache and Code Cache when Chrome is not running. Reports extension count with names, Google Update service health (informational -- MDM manages versioning), enterprise policy configuration, GPU/renderer crash loop frequency (Crashpad reports), and orphaned NativeMessaging host registry entries. Prunes stale NativeMessaging hosts automatically.
Impact Notes: Cache clear requires Chrome to be closed at scan time -- throws if Chrome is running. NativeMessaging host pruning removes orphaned registry keys only; Chrome handles missing hosts gracefully. All other steps are informational.
Additional Notes: Checks per-user, HKLM, and WOW6432Node NativeMessaging scopes. Reports ChromeVersion to DEXRecords registry.

Name: Invoke-VpnStateCollection.ps1
Description: Vendor-agnostic VPN state collection script. Identifies tunnel adapters structurally (non-hardware, not known virtual infrastructure), then collects and caches 13 VPN health values to HKLM:\Software\AirWatch\Extensions\VPN. Computes a composite health score (0-100, -1 = no client) and a leading health reason used by the remediation script and agent runbook. Designed to run on a 15-30 minute schedule; all VPN sensors read from this cache.
Impact Notes: Read-only collection and registry write. No network calls, no tunnel changes. Mines the NetworkProfile operational event log for flap/connect history.
Additional Notes: Must be scheduled as a recurring script before any VPN sensors are deployed. All 13 VPN sensors depend on this cache.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateGenericVPN.ps1
Description: Vendor-agnostic VPN remediation. Runs 6 ordered health checks and remediates the layers Windows owns: VPN support service health (RasMan / IKEEXT / BFE), tunnel MTU correction (sets to 1400), tunnel DNS flush and re-register, and orphaned route removal from inactive tunnel adapters. Explicitly does not attempt to reconnect the tunnel -- that is a vendor client operation. Step 6 (adapter bounce) ships disabled. Caches step results to HKLM:\Software\AirWatch\Extensions\VPN\Remediation.
Impact Notes: MTU change is session-scoped and reverts on client reconnect. Service restarts cause a brief gap in VPN stack availability. Step 6 (adapter bounce) drops the tunnel and cannot reconnect it -- enable only on fleets whose client auto-reconnects reliably.
Additional Notes: WhatIf=$true supported via env var. Pairs with Invoke-VpnStateCollection.ps1 for health context. Vendor-specific reconnect belongs in a separate vendor runbook.

Name: vpn_health_score.ps1
Description: Reports the composite VPN health score (0-100). -1 means no VPN client is installed -- deliberately distinct from a low score, which means a client is present and unhealthy. Read from cache written by Invoke-VpnStateCollection.ps1.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-VpnStateCollection.ps1 scheduled every 15-30 minutes.

Name: vpn_health_reason.ps1
Description: Reports the single largest deduction from the VPN health score. Values: Healthy, NoVpnClient, TunnelDown, MtuNotReducedForTunnel, MtuBelowMinimum, NoDnsOnTunnel, HighPacketDiscardRate, FrequentReconnects, IntermittentReconnects, RepeatedConnectFailures, MultipleVpnClients, CollectionError. Read from cache.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-VpnStateCollection.ps1 scheduled every 15-30 minutes.

Name: vpn_connected.ps1
Description: Reports whether an active VPN tunnel is present right now. Read live (not from cache) because a 30-minute-stale connection state is misleading. Detection is vendor-agnostic: a non-hardware adapter with a routable IPv4 address that is not known virtual infrastructure.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.

Name: vpn_tunnel_mode.ps1
Description: Reports Full, Split, or None based on default route ownership. Full = only the tunnel holds a 0.0.0.0/0 route. Split = other interfaces also hold a default route. Read live.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.

Name: vpn_adapter_name.ps1
Description: Reports the InterfaceDescription of the active tunnel adapter -- effectively which VPN client is carrying traffic right now. Empty string when no tunnel is active. Read live.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.

Name: vpn_tunnel_mtu.ps1
Description: Reports the IPv4 MTU of the active tunnel adapter. -1 means no active tunnel. Read live. A tunnel at 1500 has not accounted for encapsulation overhead and risks an MTU black hole on large transfers.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.

Name: vpn_last_connect_time.ps1
Description: Reports the timestamp of the most recent tunnel connect event within the last 24 hours. Date Time type; no value emitted when no connect event is found -- there is no safe sentinel date.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-VpnStateCollection.ps1 scheduled every 15-30 minutes.

Name: vpn_session_duration_minutes.ps1
Description: Reports minutes elapsed since the current tunnel connected. -1 means no active tunnel or the connect event predates the collection window. Value is as stale as the last collection run.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-VpnStateCollection.ps1 scheduled every 15-30 minutes.

Name: vpn_flap_count_24h.ps1
Description: Reports tunnel disconnect events in the last 24 hours. -1 means unknown. Sourced from NetworkProfile operational log (vendor-agnostic), not RasClient. Surfaces users whose tunnel drops and reconnects silently all day.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-VpnStateCollection.ps1 scheduled every 15-30 minutes.

Name: vpn_connect_failure_count_24h.ps1
Description: Reports failed VPN connection attempts in the last 24 hours from the RasClient event log. -1 means unknown. Covers the Windows built-in VPN stack only; third-party clients log failures elsewhere. Treat 0 on a third-party client as unknown, not healthy.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-VpnStateCollection.ps1 scheduled every 15-30 minutes.

Name: vpn_dns_configured.ps1
Description: Reports whether the active tunnel adapter has at least one IPv4 DNS server assigned. No value emitted when no tunnel is active (false would read as a real misconfiguration on a disconnected device). Read live.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.

Name: vpn_client_count.ps1
Description: Reports the number of VPN client tunnel adapters installed, connected or not. 0 means no client present. -1 means the adapter list could not be read. More than 1 is the signal to act on -- stacked clients contend for routes and DNS. Read live.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.

Name: vpn_discard_rate_ppm.ps1
Description: Reports discarded packets per million on the active tunnel adapter. -1 means no active tunnel. Read from cache so it agrees with the deduction applied by vpn_health_score. Lifetime average since adapter init; lags behind problems that started recently.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-VpnStateCollection.ps1 scheduled every 15-30 minutes.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateZoom.ps1
Description: Runs sequenced Zoom-specific health checks. Clears Zoom log files and data cache subdirectory when Zoom is not running. Reports Zoom updater/scheduled task health and installed version (informational). Checks Zoom Outlook COM add-in LoadBehavior across user and machine scopes. Detects sign-in/SSO failures via Zoom log pattern analysis and clears auth files (gated). Checks and corrects Windows webcam Privacy Consent Store entry for Zoom (gated).
Impact Notes: Auth file clear (gated by $AllowDestructiveActions) forces Zoom re-login. Webcam consent change (gated) sets Value=Allow in the Windows Privacy Consent Store for Zoom's exe path only -- not globally for all apps.
Additional Notes: Webcam consent uses per-app NonPackaged ConsentStore key derived from the detected Zoom exe path. Creates the key if absent.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateOneDrive.ps1
Description: Runs sequenced OneDrive-specific health checks. Restores missing HKCU auto-start Run key and starts OneDrive in the logged-on user's desktop session via a temporary Interactive scheduled task if not running. Reports business and personal account sign-in state, OneDrive error events from the Application event log (last 24h), Files On-Demand service (FileSyncHelper) health with auto-restart, and Known Folder Move (KFM) configuration via KfmFoldersProtectedNow bitmask.
Impact Notes: Starting OneDrive via a temporary scheduled task leaves no persistent artifacts (task is unregistered immediately after launch). FileSyncHelper service restart is safe. KFM, account sign-in, and sync error checks are informational only.
Additional Notes: KFM policy cross-referenced against HKLM Policies key to detect drift between policy intent and actual folder protection state.

Name: certificate_store_health.ps1
Description: Detection sensor: reports LocalMachine certificate store health as a single JSON summary -- expired/expiring-soon/weak-signature/self-signed counts in the Personal store, plus expired Root/CA counts.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: ExpiredRootOrCACount only escalates OverallStatus past a noise threshold (>20) -- a handful of expired roots is normal, unpurged Windows cruft, not itself a fault.

Name: time_sync_health.ps1
Description: Detection sensor: reports W32Time service state and clock-sync health as a single JSON summary, including phase offset and time since last good sync parsed from w32tm /query /status /verbose.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Domain-joined machines are graded against the 5-minute Kerberos clock-skew threshold; workgroup machines use a looser bar since Windows does not require them to stay tightly synced.

Name: power_profile_status.ps1
Description: Detection sensor: reports power plan/profile health as a single JSON summary -- standby mechanism (Modern Standby vs S3), active scheme/overlay, policy-lock state, battery wear, and AC/DC PROCTHROTTLEMAX.
Impact Notes: Read-only - no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Read-only counterpart to the not-yet-built Invoke-AutoRemediatePowerPlan.ps1; ProcThrottleMaxAC below 100 is the single highest-yield finding and drives OverallStatus to Critical.

Name: logon_duration_measure.ps1
Description: Self-contained one-time/run-once sensor that mines the same event logs as Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 directly and returns every logon phase timing as a single compressed JSON object -- no collector script, scheduled task, or registry cache required. Requires Workspace ONE Intelligence's one-time sensor run capability; MUST NOT be scheduled as a recurring sensor.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. Self-enforces a 25 s deadline (30 s UEM hard ceiling for one-time sensors); unattempted phases report -4 (TimedOut) rather than blocking past their budget.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -3 Log disabled, -4 Timed out. Printer/task phases report LogDisabled until Enable-LogonAuditLogs.ps1 (or Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 -DeployMode ConfigureLogging) has run.

Name: Enable-LogonAuditLogs.ps1
Description: Standalone script that enables the two Windows event logs disabled by default but required for full logon-phase coverage: Microsoft-Windows-PrintService/Operational and Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational. Extracted from Measure-LogonDuration.ps1's Enable-DEXAuditLogs so it can be run independently ahead of logon_duration_measure.ps1. Idempotent via a registry marker shared with Measure-LogonDuration.ps1 -DeployMode ConfigureLogging; -Force re-runs regardless.
Impact Notes: Configuration change only (wevtutil sl /e:true on two optional logs). No user-visible interruption. Requires local administrator / SYSTEM context.
Additional Notes: Run once per device image before relying on printer mapping / logon task metrics from either logon duration sensor.

Name: printer_inventory.ps1
Description: Lists every printer registered with the local print spooler as a single JSON object -- name, driver, port, default/shared/network flags, offline state, and current status/error condition (e.g. low toner, paper jam). Read-only counterpart to Invoke-AutoRemediatePrinter.ps1's installed-printer and condition checks.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: SYSTEM context enumerates the machine-wide spooler; a network printer connected only inside the interactive user's own session may not appear if never registered at the machine level.

Name: profile_size_inventory.ps1
Description: One-time/run-once sensor listing every non-special local user profile -- size on disk (native .NET DirectoryInfo walk, no Get-ChildItem), and days since last login -- as a single JSON object. Read-only inventory counterpart to Start-UserProfileCleanup.ps1; unlike that script it reports ALL non-special profiles, not just domain/non-enrollment candidates.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. Self-enforces a 25 s wall-clock deadline shared across all profiles (30 s UEM hard ceiling); profiles not yet sized when the deadline hits report -4 (TimedOut) rather than a partial size.
Additional Notes: -1 Unknown (no LastUseTime recorded), -4 Timed out (budget exhausted before this profile's size was walked). Top-level Truncated:true means not every profile finished before the deadline.

Name: logon_folder_redirection_map.ps1
Description: Recurring sensor listing every Folder Redirection-eligible known folder (Desktop, Documents, Pictures, Downloads, AppData\Roaming, etc.) for the active interactive user and its current target path, as a single JSON object. Registry-only (HKU SID Shell Folders / User Shell Folders) -- no disk enumeration or network calls -- so unlike profile_size_inventory.ps1 this does not need one-time classification. Complements the existing FolderRedirectMs timing signal with the actual target paths.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Redirected:true means the resolved path is a UNC path (\\\\server\\share\\...); OneDrive Known Folder Move also changes these same registry values but points to a local path, so it correctly reports Redirected:false.

Name: logon_folder_redirection_latency_probe.ps1
Description: One-time/run-once companion to logon_folder_redirection_map.ps1. For every UNC-redirected known folder, times a bounded TCP:445 connect to the target server (fast, firewall-friendly reachability + latency proxy) and a bounded folder-existence check, then combines reachability/latency with a static per-folder impact weight (AppData Roaming/Desktop/Start Menu weighted highest since they're read synchronously at logon) into a per-folder and overall Folder Redirection risk score.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. Makes outbound TCP:445 connection attempts only to servers already named in the user's own redirected-folder registry values; every network/file-existence check is individually bounded (1.5 s each) and the whole run self-enforces a 15 s wall-clock budget (30 s UEM hard ceiling).
Additional Notes: LikelyServedByCache:true (server unreachable but path still resolves instantly) indicates Offline Files (CSC) is serving the folder locally rather than over the network. Severity: NotApplicable (not redirected), Normal, Elevated (ConnectMs >= 150), Critical (unreachable), or TimedOut (budget exhausted before this folder was probed, RiskScore -4).

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgent.ps1
Description: Tier 1 fleet-wide Operations Manager agent health sweep. Runs 14 ordered checks (service state, startup delay, management group registration, MS connectivity on TCP 5723, config cache freshness, state folder size, ESENT store errors, runtime footprint, connector failures, workflow health, channel certificate, agent version, time skew, optional sub-services) and auto-remediates only two: starting a stopped HealthService and flushing DNS. Every other step reports and names the Tier 2 spin-off that would address it. Agent-side only -- server-side findings are stated explicitly and not acted on. Caches all metrics plus a 0-100 health score to HKLM:\Software\AirWatch\Extensions\SCOM for the sensors to read.
Impact Notes: Starts HealthService and sets its start type to Automatic; flushes the DNS resolver cache. No user-visible interruption. All destructive operations are deliberately excluded and delegated to the opt-in Tier 2 scripts.
Additional Notes: WhatIf=true supported via env var. Guard clause exits 0 and writes AgentInstalled=0 / HealthScore=-1 when no agent is present, so unmonitored devices are identifiable rather than absent. Reads the Operations Manager event log once and buckets it in memory; sizes folders with Scripting.FileSystemObject. NOT DEPLOYABLE -- 48,336 characters against the 32,767 UEM limit. Retained as the combined reference implementation; deploy Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgentPart1/2/3.ps1 instead.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMHealthServiceCache.ps1
Description: Tier 2 opt-in DESTRUCTIVE Health Service State flush. Stops HealthService, renames the Health Service State folder, restarts the service and waits for the agent to re-download configuration from its management server. Rename-then-delete, so a failed restart rolls back to the original state. Five gates must all pass: ConfirmHighImpact set, agent installed with no install in progress, management server reachable on its configured port, a real flush signal present (stale config / ESENT errors / oversized folder -- not age alone), and the 7-day cooldown elapsed.
Impact Notes: DESTRUCTIVE. Deletes accumulated agent state including queued data not yet uploaded to the management server; that data is lost. Every flushed agent re-downloads its full configuration, so a broad simultaneous rollout is a synchronised load spike on the management group and its operational database. Deploy to targeted rings with randomisation, never fleet-wide.
Additional Notes: REQUIRES ConfirmHighImpact=true env var; absent or unparseable means nothing is flushed (fails closed). WhatIf=true supported. Launcher/payload pattern -- copies itself to C:\ProgramData\AirWatch\Extensions\SCOM and runs via a one-shot SYSTEM scheduled task, so an AV/EDR exclusion on that path is required or the payload silently no-ops.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMMonitoringHost.ps1
Description: Tier 2 opt-in Operations Manager agent recycle. Restarts HealthService when the agent process set (HealthService + MonitoringHost) shows sustained high CPU or memory. Deliberately has no ConfirmHighImpact gate -- recycling restarts only the agent own service, nothing else depends on it and no data is at risk. Instead it requires two independent load samples 45 seconds apart plus a 20-hour cooldown, and skips agents that started or received configuration in the last 15 minutes because that load burst is expected.
Impact Notes: Restarts the Operations Manager agent service. In-flight workflows are dropped and the agent rebuilds runtime state on start; monitoring has a short gap. No user-visible interruption and no data deletion. A device that keeps re-qualifying has a management pack scoping problem the recycle cannot fix.
Additional Notes: WhatIf=true supported via env var. No ConfirmHighImpact gate by design -- gating it alongside the genuinely destructive scripts would train admins to set that variable reflexively. Launcher/payload pattern requiring an AV/EDR exclusion on C:\ProgramData\AirWatch\Extensions\SCOM. Particularly relevant on VDI/Horizon/AVD session hosts where agent footprint is multiplied by session density.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMClonedIdentity.ps1
Description: Tier 2 opt-in DESTRUCTIVE agent identity reset for cloned devices. Removes image-baked Health Service State carrying a parent image identity so the agent re-registers with the management group under its own. Requires BOTH confirmations independently: agent state predating OS install beyond a 30-minute grace window (image-baked), AND at least 3 management server rejection events in 24 hours. Either signal alone aborts -- image-baked state is harmless on a machine that later registered successfully, and rejections alone usually mean an approval problem rather than a clone.
Impact Notes: DESTRUCTIVE, highest blast radius of the three Tier 2 scripts. Deletes agent state and changes agent identity. WRONG TOOL for non-persistent VDI -- the reset is discarded with the session and the next clone reproduces the problem; fix the parent image instead. The management server may still need an administrator to approve the new registration and clean up the stale duplicate, which this script cannot do.
Additional Notes: REQUIRES ConfirmHighImpact=true env var; absent or unparseable means nothing is reset (fails closed). WhatIf=true supported. 14-day cooldown, the longest of the three, because a repeat reset means the diagnosis was wrong. Launcher/payload pattern requiring an AV/EDR exclusion on C:\ProgramData\AirWatch\Extensions\SCOM.

Name: scom_agent_health_score.ps1
Description: Reports the composite Operations Manager agent health score (0-100). -1 means no agent is installed -- deliberately distinct from a low score, which means an agent is present and unhealthy. Read from cache written by Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgent.ps1.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgent.ps1 scheduled (writes the cache this reads). Filter -1 out before averaging or ranking; a fleet of devices that never had the agent installed will otherwise drag every average down.

Name: scom_agent_health_reason.ps1
Description: Reports the single largest deduction from the SCOM agent health score. Values: Healthy, NoAgentInstalled, HealthServiceStopped, ManagementServerUnreachable, AgentNotRegistered, NoManagementGroup, ConnectorAuthenticationFailure, HealthServiceStoreCorruption, ConfigurationCacheStale, AgentRuntimeFootprintHigh, ChannelCertificateProblem, TimeSkew, WorkflowsUnloaded, HealthServiceStateOversized, MultiHomedAgent, IntermittentConnectivity. Read from cache.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgent.ps1 scheduled (writes the cache this reads). Exclude NoAgentInstalled before ranking. ManagementServerUnreachable, AgentNotRegistered, ConnectorAuthenticationFailure and ChannelCertificateProblem are server-side or PKI conditions no agent-side script can clear -- alert on the fleet-wide count of each rather than per device.

Name: scom_management_server_reachable.ps1
Description: Reports whether the agent configured management server answered on its configured port (5723 by default) at the last sweep. Read from cache, never probed live -- a recurring sensor must not make network calls, and the cached answer matches the one the health score was calculated from.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgent.ps1 scheduled (writes the cache this reads). Deliberately emits NO value when it cannot tell, rather than false -- a missing cache means the sweep has not run, not that the management server is down, and any boolean fallback would manufacture a fleet-wide outage out of a scheduling problem. False across many devices at once is a management-group or network incident.

Name: scom_agent_version.ps1
Description: Reports the four-part file version of the installed Operations Manager agent, e.g. 10.19.10552.0. Empty string means no agent or the version could not be read. Read from cache.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgent.ps1 scheduled (writes the cache this reads). Returned as String -- string comparison does NOT order versions correctly (10.19.10552.0 sorts below 10.19.1082.0), so group by exact value rather than filtering on greater-than. Rough mapping: 8.x = SCOM 2012 R2, 10.19.x = 2019, 10.22.x = 2022, 10.23.x = 2025. The MMA binary is also the Log Analytics agent, so a populated version does not prove the device reports to a SCOM management group.

Name: scom_config_age_hours.ps1
Description: Reports hours since the agent connector configuration cache was last written, as at the last sweep. A climbing value means the agent is running on stale management pack configuration -- alerting on yesterday rules and silent about anything added since. -1 means not measured. Read from cache.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgent.ps1 scheduled (writes the cache this reads). Age alone is not corruption -- a stable management group that has not changed a management pack in a week legitimately shows an old cache, which is why the HealthServiceCache flush script requires a corroborating signal. The value advances in sweep-sized steps, not continuously.

Name: scom_state_folder_mb.ps1
Description: Reports the size in MB of the agent Health Service State folder at the last sweep. -1 means not measured. Cached rather than measured live because walking that tree is far too slow for a recurring sensor. Read from cache.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgent.ps1 scheduled (writes the cache this reads). Primary targeting metric for Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMHealthServiceCache.ps1 -- sort descending and deploy the flush to the top of the fleet only, never fleet-wide. On a small-disk VDI or thin laptop this is genuine capacity, and the 1536 MB default threshold is already too generous there.

Name: scom_monitoringhost_memory_mb.ps1
Description: Reports the combined working set in MB of HealthService.exe plus every MonitoringHost.exe child at the last sweep. -1 means not measured. Read from cache.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: Requires Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgent.ps1 scheduled (writes the cache this reads). The metric that matters on VDI/Horizon/AVD, where the same agent footprint is multiplied by session count and surfaces as host memory pressure rather than as a SCOM problem. A single high value is not a fault -- management packs legitimately spike the agent during discovery; sustained growth across samples is the signal.

Name: scom_agent_health.ps1
Description: Self-contained one-time/run-once sensor returning the complete Operations Manager agent picture as a single compact JSON object -- every metric the recurring Sensors/ folder exposes plus failover server count, store DB size, per-category event counts, certificate expiry, service uptime and a Findings array. Does its own detection and reads no cache, so it works on a device where the sweep has never run. Mines the Operations Manager event log and makes one bounded TCP probe to the management server. Covers all 14 sweep steps in one pass. Requires the Workspace ONE Intelligence one-time sensor run capability; MUST NOT be scheduled as a recurring sensor.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. Makes one bounded TCP connect (3 s) to the management server already named in the agent own registry configuration. Self-enforces a 25 s deadline (30 s UEM hard ceiling); phases skipped by that deadline report -4 rather than running past budget.
Additional Notes: Sentinels: -1 Unknown, -2 Not applicable, -4 Timed out. HealthScore is the one exception -- it reports -1 for no agent installed to match the sweep and scom_agent_health_score so the two sources can be unioned. When TimedOut is true, HealthScore is a floor not a verdict; filter on it before trending. Scoring mirrors the sweep deduction table condition for condition, with one documented divergence: TimeSkew here is driven by time-sync age (registry) rather than measured clock skew, because a sensor must not launch w32tm.exe. Kept in a separate OneTimeSensor/ folder so it is not scheduled recurring by mistake. Not usable until the DEX one-time sensor run capability ships.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgentPart1.ps1
Description: Part 1 of 3 of the Tier 1 Operations Manager agent health sweep. Runs steps 1-5: HealthService service state (AUTO -- sc.exe config/start), startup delay, management group registration, management server connectivity on TCP 5723 (AUTO -- flush DNS only), and configuration cache freshness. Caches ManagementServer, ManagementGroupCount, ConfigAgeHours, MsReachable and ServiceRunning to HKLM:\Software\AirWatch\Extensions\SCOM for Part 3 to score. The sweep is split into three script objects because combined it is 48,336 characters against the 32,767 UEM limit.
Impact Notes: Starts HealthService and sets its start type to Automatic; flushes the DNS resolver cache. No user-visible interruption.
Additional Notes: Deploy alongside Part 2, both before Part 3. WhatIf=true supported via env var. Guard clause exits 0 and writes AgentInstalled=0 / HealthScore=-1 when no agent is present.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgentPart2.ps1
Description: Part 2 of 3 of the Tier 1 Operations Manager agent health sweep. Runs steps 6-10: Health Service State folder size, Health Service Store database (ESENT 477/490/623), agent runtime footprint (MonitoringHost CPU/RAM), connector connectivity failures (20070/20071/21006/21016) and workflow health (1103/1102/4001/21405). Owns the single bucketed pass over the Operations Manager event log shared by steps 9 and 10. Remediates nothing -- each finding names the Tier 2 spin-off that would act.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. The most expensive of the three parts because of the event-log mining; give it the longest UEM timeout.
Additional Notes: Deploy alongside Part 1, both before Part 3. WhatIf=true supported. Folder sizes use Scripting.FileSystemObject, not Get-ChildItem -Recurse.

Name: Invoke-AutoRemediateSCOMAgentPart3.ps1
Description: Part 3 of 3 of the Tier 1 Operations Manager agent health sweep. Runs steps 11-14: channel certificate health, agent version, time synchronisation skew and optional agent sub-services. ALSO COMPUTES THE HEALTH SCORE for the whole sweep by reading back every metric Parts 1 and 2 cached and applying the full 14-rule deduction table, then writes the aggregate Status, HealthScore, HealthReason and counts that all the recurring sensors read.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device.
Additional Notes: MUST RUN LAST -- schedule at least 15 minutes after Parts 1 and 2. If Part1RunTime or Part2RunTime is missing or older than $StalePartHours (26h) it publishes HealthScore=-1 / HealthReason=IncompleteSweep and ScoreComplete=0 rather than a partial score, because missing metrics cannot deduct and a partial score is always too high. WhatIf=true supported.

Name: scom_agent_health_score_standalone.ps1
Description: Standalone composite Operations Manager agent health score (0-100), computed live on the device with no cache and no sweep script deployed. Applies the same point values, thresholds and reason names as the sweep, over the subset of rules a recurring sensor can evaluate: service state (40), no management group (20), stale config cache (15), high runtime footprint (15), channel certificate problem (15), stale time sync (15), oversized state folder (10), multi-homed (5). Maximum deduction 130 against the sweep 235. -1 means no agent installed or the measurement failed.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. No network calls and no external processes.
Additional Notes: Requires nothing -- no cache, no sweep script. Deploy this OR scom_agent_health_score.ps1, never both: two sensors reporting the same attribute under different names doubles the sensor queue for one number. THE TWO SCORES ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER and must not be pooled -- this one cannot see the management server or the event logs, so ManagementServerUnreachable, AgentNotRegistered, ConnectorAuthenticationFailure, HealthServiceStoreCorruption, WorkflowsUnloaded and IntermittentConnectivity are all invisible to it and a device that cannot report at all still scores 100. Run OneTimeSensor/scom_agent_health.ps1 once against the same fleet to measure how much is being missed. Measured 39-266 ms on a synthetic agent fixture.

Name: scom_agent_health_reason_standalone.ps1
Description: Standalone companion to scom_agent_health_score_standalone.ps1 -- the single largest deduction, computed live with no cache. Values: HealthServiceStopped, NoManagementGroup, ConfigurationCacheStale, AgentRuntimeFootprintHigh, ChannelCertificateProblem, TimeSyncStale, HealthServiceStateOversized, MultiHomedAgent, HealthyLocal, NoAgentInstalled, or empty string on failure.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. No network calls and no external processes.
Additional Notes: Requires nothing -- no cache, no sweep script. Deploy this OR scom_agent_health_reason.ps1, never both, and always deploy it WITH its score sensor. Two values differ deliberately from the cached twin: HealthyLocal rather than Healthy, because this sensor cannot see the management server or the event logs; and TimeSyncStale rather than TimeSkew, because measuring real clock offset needs w32tm.exe and a sensor may not launch a process. Do not merge either with the sweep equivalent in a report. Only the largest deduction is reported -- a device with four findings shows one.

Name: scom_healthservice_running_standalone.ps1
Description: Reports whether the Operations Manager agent is actually monitoring: HealthService Running AND start type Automatic. Measured live, no cache. Start type is part of the test on purpose -- a HealthService running under Manual or Disabled is monitoring now and silently gone after the next reboot. Emits no value when there is no agent at all; false when registry keys exist but the service does not, which is a partial install or partial removal.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. No network calls and no external processes.
Additional Notes: Requires nothing -- no cache, no sweep script. NEW, not a replacement: the sweep caches this as ServiceRunning but exposes it only through the health score, so there is no cached twin to conflict with. Same test as the sweep 40-point HealthServiceStopped deduction, so the two datasets line up. Deliberately emits NO value on an agentless device rather than false -- any boolean there would read as a real negative finding. A fleet running the sweep should rarely show false twice in a row, because Part 1 repairs this automatically; a device that does has a start failure the sweep could not fix.

Name: scom_management_group_count_standalone.ps1
Description: Number of management groups the Operations Manager agent is assigned to, read live from the agent own registry. Read as three populations, not as a magnitude: 0 means installed but unassigned and monitoring nothing, 1 is normal, 2 or more is multi-homed and runs a full workflow set per group. -1 means not measured.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. No network calls and no external processes.
Additional Notes: Requires nothing -- no cache, no sweep script. NEW, not a replacement: the sweep caches ManagementGroupCount but exposes it only through the health score. On an endpoint fleet a 0 is usually a Log Analytics / Azure Monitor install of the same MMA binary rather than a broken SCOM agent -- cross-reference scom_agent_version_standalone.ps1 before raising it with the SCOM team. A group counted here has a registry key, which is not the same as having a parent management server assigned; an agent configured but never approved shows 1 and still cannot report. That distinction needs the sweep or the one-time sensor.

Name: scom_cert_expiry_days_standalone.ps1
Description: Days until the Operations Manager agent channel certificate expires, read live from LocalMachine\My. Negative values other than the sentinels are real and mean already expired. Sentinels: -1 not measured, -9999 a serial number is configured but no matching certificate exists (the agent cannot authenticate at all), -9998 not applicable because no channel certificate is configured, which is expected for Kerberos-authenticated domain-joined agents.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. No network calls and no external processes.
Additional Notes: Requires nothing -- no cache, no sweep script. NEW, not a replacement: the sweep caches CertExpiryDays but exposes it only through the health score. Sort ascending and triage order falls out correctly -- missing certificate, then expired, then expiring, then healthy -- with the not-applicable population parked at -9998 where a less-than-30 filter would otherwise swallow it. Filter -9998 out before counting anything. Certificate renewal is a PKI action; nothing on the endpoint can fix a lapsed channel certificate, which is why the sweep reports this step and never remediates it.

Name: scom_agent_version_standalone.ps1
Description: Standalone twin of scom_agent_version.ps1. Four-part file version of the installed Operations Manager agent, read live from the agent own registry instead of from the sweep cache. Empty string means no agent or the version could not be read.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. No network calls and no external processes.
Additional Notes: Requires nothing -- no cache, no sweep script. Deploy this OR scom_agent_version.ps1, never both. Read order is CurrentVersion, then ProductVersion, then the FileVersion of HealthService.exe -- the binary is last rather than first because after a failed or partial upgrade the file on disk is not necessarily the version that is registered. String comparison does NOT order versions correctly; group by exact value. The MMA binary is also the Log Analytics agent, so a populated version does not prove the device reports to a SCOM management group.

Name: scom_config_age_hours_standalone.ps1
Description: Standalone twin of scom_config_age_hours.ps1. Hours since the agent connector configuration cache was last written, measured live at sample time rather than as at the last sweep. -1 means not measured. Rounded to whole hours.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. No network calls and no external processes.
Additional Notes: Requires nothing -- no cache, no sweep script. Deploy this OR scom_config_age_hours.ps1, never both. Strictly better than the cached twin in one respect -- the value is continuous rather than advancing in sweep-sized steps -- but a device will show at most a one-hour difference between the two, well inside the 24h staleness threshold either reads against. Age alone is not corruption: a stable management group that has not changed a management pack in a week legitimately shows an old cache, and this sensor cannot see the corroborating signals the flush script requires.

Name: scom_state_folder_mb_standalone.ps1
Description: Standalone twin of scom_state_folder_mb.ps1. Size in MB of the agent Health Service State folder, measured live with Scripting.FileSystemObject. -1 means not measured -- it is not zero and it is not small.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. No network calls and no external processes.
Additional Notes: Requires nothing -- no cache, no sweep script. Deploy this OR scom_state_folder_mb.ps1, never both. The one standalone sensor here with an unbounded worst case: FSO walks the subtree in native code and returns in well under a second in practice, because state-folder bloat is almost always a handful of very large files rather than a large file count -- but a folder pathological in file count would be slower, and a blocking COM call cannot be time-boxed from inside a sensor without a thread, which sensors may not create. On a fleet known to have deep per-workflow cache sprawl, deploy the cached twin against the sweep instead; a script has the budget for it and a sensor does not.

Name: scom_monitoringhost_memory_mb_standalone.ps1
Description: Standalone twin of scom_monitoringhost_memory_mb.ps1. Combined working set in MB of HealthService.exe plus every MonitoringHost.exe child, measured live at sample time. -1 means no agent process is running.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. No network calls and no external processes.
Additional Notes: Requires nothing -- no cache, no sweep script. Deploy this OR scom_monitoringhost_memory_mb.ps1, never both. Note the sentinel differs in meaning from the cached twin: there -1 also covers the sweep not having run, here the only cause is that no agent process exists, which usually means HealthService is stopped -- confirm with scom_healthservice_running_standalone.ps1. Sampling live makes this MORE likely to catch a legitimate management pack discovery spike than the cached twin, not less; sustained growth across consecutive samples is the signal.

Name: device_is_virtual.ps1
Description: Reports whether the device is a virtual machine (true) or physical hardware (false). Correlates four independent families of evidence and treats any single hit as conclusive: SMBIOS firmware identity read from HKLM:\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System\BIOS, the same identity independently via Win32_ComputerSystem and Win32_BIOS, ACPI table OEM vendor IDs under HKLM:\HARDWARE\ACPI (which survive hypervisors configured to mask their SMBIOS strings), and guest-tool services and paravirtual drivers that Windows does not ship in-box, plus the Hyper-V guest parameter key. Covers VMware, Hyper-V, Azure, VirtualBox, QEMU, KVM, Proxmox, Xen, Citrix Hypervisor, Nutanix AHV, Parallels, Amazon EC2 (Nitro and Xen generations), Google Compute Engine, OpenStack, oVirt/RHV, bhyve, Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, Apple Virtualization and Virtual PC, with a generic catch for hypervisors that identify only as Virtual something.
Impact Notes: Read-only -- no changes made to the device. No network calls and no external processes.
Additional Notes: Requires nothing -- reads local firmware and registry state only, no network, no external processes, no writes. Emits NO value when neither the firmware registry key nor WMI can be read, because false is the more damaging guess there (it silently adds a device to the physical population). DELIBERATELY DOES NOT USE HypervisorPresent, which is wrong in both directions: every Windows device with VBS, Credential Guard, Core Isolation, WSL2, Windows Sandbox or the Hyper-V role reports true while physical, and the VMware guest this was developed on reports FALSE because VMware does not surface the CPUID hypervisor bit unless nested virtualisation is enabled. Also ignores the vmic-star, Vmbus, hvservice and hyperkbd services -- all six exist on stock Windows regardless of platform and were present on the VMware development guest, so a detector keying on them calls every Windows machine a Hyper-V VM. Disk device strings are excluded too: a mounted VHDX on physical hardware presents as Ven_Msft and Prod_Virtual_Disk. A physical host running Hyper-V or VMware Workstation correctly reports false; nested guests report true. Verified against a 25-case matrix (18 hypervisor and cloud platforms including SMBIOS-masked variants, 6 physical negatives including a VBS-enabled Windows 11 device and an Intel Xeon box that probes the xen token boundary, and the unreadable case) plus a live run on a VMware guest at 80-94 ms warm, 640 ms on the first WMI call.
